teaser: Rusk fought the new rule and wrote an adult wording again, and the farm watched the plant do nothing with it: Bea held the open green journal up at the wall and no leaf moved, and then she held up a lamp and the whole crown turned to it. The officer stood at the roots on the third morning, got as far as the first sound of the name and could not say it, and the law took the next price out of the same hand — a finger, with no pain and no blood. The plant was never angry and was never listening; the count has restarted this morning, and three days from now the officer loses an eye.

options.label: Say the name anyway
options.prompt: Continue the story: have the crew push Officer Rusk to say the forbidden name at the roots before the third day is out, and show what the farm does when the dead child's name is finally spoken over the soil.

options.label: Close the green journal
options.prompt: Continue the story: have the crew argue about shutting the green journal so that no line can be written and no price taken, and show what the law does on a farm where the requests are no longer written down.

options.label: Search for another name
options.prompt: Continue the story: send Meren into the low ring's records to find out whether any child of Hesper died before the last funeral, and show what she finds and who tries to stop her.
